transcript.text: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?

OE means the machine has not been able to drain within its allowed time. With water still in the drum, the usual causes are a blocked filter/foreign object, a kink or blockage in the drain hose or household waste pipe, and less often the drain pump itself. You do not need to open the filter straight into a flooded kitchen. That flap is the filter access, and opening it with a full drum can release a lot of water. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Check the grey drain hose at the back all the way to the sink waste or standpipe. Make sure it is not kinked, squashed behind the machine, or pushed into a blocked-looking waste connection. Correcting a kink may be all that is needed. 2. Plug it back in, select Drain/Spin if available, and listen near the lower front while it attempts to empty. A humming/straining noise points more to a blockage in the filter, pump or hose; complete silence makes a pump or its electrical supply more possible. 3. If you do decide to empty it through the lower access, use the machine manual’s residual-water draining method first. Once the water is controlled, the filter is still the first place to inspect for coins, hair grips, lint or buttons. If the hose is clear and it hums but no water leaves, a blockage remains more likely than a failed pump. If the filter and hose prove clear but it still will not drain, that is the point to arrange an engineer for the pump or an internal hose obstruction.
Ok, the machine was pushed right back against the wall and the hose was squashed behind it. I've pulled it out and straightened it. Do I just try a spin again now?

OE means it timed out without draining, and a squashed hose is a very plausible reason for it. Stay nearby for the first minute or two and check the hose does not kink again or leak where it joins the waste pipe. If it pumps the water out and completes, the hose restriction was the cause; leave enough clearance behind the machine when pushing it back. If it still shows OE or leaves water in the drum, switch it off and unplug it again. The next most likely cause is a blocked filter or an obstruction at the pump, so it would need emptying by the controlled residual-water method before opening that lower filter—not simply unscrewing it with a full drum.

I tried the spin again. It drained a little slower than normal and then showed OE again. Water's still in the drum. I'm still not unscrewing that filter myself, and I don't want water all over the laminate.

Don’t unscrew the filter with the drum still full if you are not comfortable controlling the water — that is exactly how the floor gets flooded. Because straightening the crushed hose allowed it to drain only a little, there is probably still a restriction. The most likely cause is a blocked pump filter or something caught just behind it; a partial blockage in the hose/waste connection is the next possibility. A failed drain pump is possible, but should not be assumed until those blockages have been excluded. At this point, the sensible option is a washing-machine engineer. Ask them to drain the machine in a controlled way, clear and inspect the pump filter and pump path, then check the external drain hose and household waste connection before condemning the pump. Keep the machine switched off and unplugged until it is dealt with, and leave it pulled forward enough that the hose cannot be crushed again.
